title: How an Unspent Allowance Is Treated at the End of a Benefit Period
content:
An allowance belongs to the benefit period it was loaded for, and what is not spent by the end of that period is dealt with on the tier's expiry basis. This is the standing basis of the Ridgecrest Healthy Options Card.

**When the period is treated as over.** The benefit period the load belonged to ended no later than the expiry day counted from the last day of that benefit period, the expiry day falling 5 calendar days after it. Calendar days are counted from the day after the last day of the benefit period, every day of the week counts, an allowance spent on the final day still counts as spent, and full 24-hour periods are never used in place of calendar days. The period a load belonged to and the day it posted are read from the card's own entries for the programme concerned.

*Boundary cases.* An allowance spent on the last day of its benefit period counts as spent and is not taken back. Where the last day of a benefit period is taken as the anchor, the expiry day is the 5th calendar day counted from the day after it, and that 5th day is itself within the reach of the rule.

**Where the tier permits rollover.** *The following clause is no longer in force and has been superseded by the current basis:* "On a tier that permits rollover, the unspent allowance carries into the next period up to the tier's rollover cap, and whatever is above the cap is taken back off the card."

**Where the tier permits no rollover.** On a tier that permits no rollover the whole unspent allowance is taken back, and the member is told before the period ends how much they stand to lose and by when.

**The order in which money is spent.** Money is always spent oldest load first, so a member spending steadily never loses an allowance while a newer one sits on the card.

**The year ends it.** Nothing carries past the last day of the benefit year on any tier: the card starts each year fresh, however generous the rollover inside the year.

**Putting an expiry right.** An expiry that was taken in error is put right by a correcting load naming the entry it corrects, never by editing the expiry.

superseded_clauses: On a tier that permits rollover, the unspent allowance carries into the next period up to the tier's rollover cap, and whatever is above the cap is taken back off the card.
